title: Moving Stones Until Consecutive II
description:
Stones sit on an infinite number line at the distinct integer positions given in `stones`.

A stone is an **endpoint stone** if it is at the smallest or the largest position. In one move you pick up an endpoint stone and place it on an unoccupied integer position such that it is **no longer** an endpoint stone (that is, strictly between the new smallest and largest remaining positions). The game ends when the stones occupy consecutive positions, after which no move is possible.

Return an array `[minimumMoves, maximumMoves]`: the fewest and the most moves you can make before the game ends.

**Example 1:**
```
Input: stones = [1,5,6,12]
Output: [2,5]
Explanation: Minimum: move 1 to 7, then 12 to 8, for [5,6,7,8]. Maximum: move 1 to 7, then 5 to 8, 6 to 9, 7 to 10 and 8 to 11, ending at [9,10,11,12] after 5 moves.
```

**Example 2:**
```
Input: stones = [6,5,4,3,10]
Output: [2,3]
Explanation: Minimum: move 3 to 8, then 10 to 7, for [4,5,6,7,8]. Maximum: move 3 to 7, then 4 to 8, then 5 to 9, for [6,7,8,9,10].
```

**Example 3:**
```
Input: stones = [100,101,104,102,103]
Output: [0,0]
Explanation: The stones already occupy 100-104 consecutively, so no move can be made.
```

examples.explanation: Minimum: move 1 to 7, then 12 to 8, for [5,6,7,8]. Maximum: move 1 to 7, then 5 to 8, 6 to 9, 7 to 10 and 8 to 11, ending at [9,10,11,12] after 5 moves.
Minimum: move 3 to 8, then 10 to 7, for [4,5,6,7,8]. Maximum: move 3 to 7, then 4 to 8, then 5 to 9, for [6,7,8,9,10].
The stones already occupy 100-104 consecutively, so no move can be made.

constraints: All values in stones are distinct
solution_approach: Simulating moves with search is exponential. Sort the stones (n of them). For the maximum: the first move must abandon one endpoint, discarding either the gap stones[1] - stones[0] - 1 or stones[n-1] - stones[n-2] - 1; after that every empty slot inside the span can be filled one at a time, so max = (stones[n-1] - stones[0] + 1 - n) - min(both edge gaps). For the minimum: slide a window over the sorted stones looking for the target block of n consecutive positions [stones[i], stones[i] + n - 1]; the moves needed are n minus the number of stones already inside. The one exception is when n - 1 stones are already consecutive and the last stone is more than one slot away, which needs 2 moves rather than 1. Sorting dominates: O(n log n) time and O(1) extra space (O(n) if sorting is not in place).
hints: Sort the stones. Think separately about the most moves and the fewest moves.

For the maximum, the first move discards the gap at one end; afterwards you can fill every remaining empty slot one move at a time. For the minimum, consider a window of n consecutive positions and count how many stones already lie inside it.

Use two pointers so that stones[j] - stones[i] < n; the cost is n - (j - i + 1), except when j - i + 1 = n - 1 and the window is already consecutive (stones[j] - stones[i] = n - 2), where the cost is 2 instead of 1.
follow_up_questions: Why does the special case of n - 1 consecutive stones need two moves instead of one?
How does the problem change if any stone (not only endpoints) may be moved?
